subject: Proposal: Move from quarterly invoices to annual committed term + staggered true-up
body:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@ecosense.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ecosense Procurement <procurement@ecosense.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring annual committed pricing vs quarterly billing

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our finance and platform teams want to evaluate moving away from quarterly invoicing/consumption to an annual committed model (with a true-up). The goals are: predictability for budgeting, a single invoice, and better unit pricing if we can commit.

Primary asks from our side:
- Targeted annual spend range for first-year commitment: $400k–$600k (we expect bursty usage early).
- If we commit to a 2-year term, what incremental discount do you offer?
- Can we get a staggered ramp (lower effective commit in Q1, scale up by Q3) plus a true-up cadence?
- Need clear break clauses for underutilization and a safe harbor for production performance issues.

We'd like to move quickly; procurement wants an initial commercial proposal and indicative legal terms to review by end of next week.

Attaching a short usage export for the last 6 months (CSV) to give you a sense.

—Liam

Attachment: ecosense_usage_jan-jun.csv (csv)

----
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@ecosense.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual committed pricing vs quarterly billing

Hi Liam — really appreciate the usage dump, that helps. Attached is an initial commercial outline and practical ramp options for a move to an annual committed structure. High level:

- Option A: 12-month annual commit (single invoice, quarterly true-up)
  - Indicative first-year committed spend: $500k
  - Unit discount vs current list: 15%
  - True-up cadence: quarterly (30 days after quarter close)
  - Staggered ramp: effective commit recognized 50% in Q1, 75% in Q2, 100% in Q3—helps preserve credit for early underutilization.

- Option B: 24-month annualized (2-year) commit with deeper discount
  - Year 1 commit: $450k; Year 2 commit: $750k (assumed growth profile)
  - Effective blended discount: 20% on year 1, 25% on year 2 if usage meets thresholds
  - True-up: semi-annual for year 1 (to reduce admin), quarterly in year 2
  - Break clause: standard 60-day notice at renewal with a mid-term true-up if usage < 60% of committed run rate for two consecutive quarters

We can include a performance credit schedule tied to latency/availability SLOs (small % of monthly invoice) so you have a safety net if production-level issues reduce value.

I've attached "Redwood_Annual_Proposal_0621.pdf" and a link to our standard commercial terms. Ben and Aditya are looped in for any pricing flexibility. Let us know which option you'd like us to firm up and we'll produce a formal SOW + numbers sheet.

Thanks,
Priya

Attachments: Redwood_Annual_Proposal_0621.pdf, Redwood_Terms_v3.docx

----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@ecosense.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual committed pricing vs quarterly billing

Liam — quick follow. We reviewed the usage profile and Priya's options. For a 24-month commit we can be more aggressive on concessions to help your ramp:

- 2-year commitment incentive: additional 5% credit applied as true-up protection in year 1 (applies only to over-commit protection, not to base discount).
- If Ecosense agrees to a staged scale (50/75/100 as Priya noted), we can accept a quarterly true-up with a cushion: first two quarters are credit-protected up to 30% underutilization (we'll convert unused committed spend into a one-time credit).
- For procurement simplicity, we propose a single annual invoice delivered at contract effective date with quarterly accounting true-ups (simplifies AR).
- We will include a 90-day SLA remediation window and a capped service credit pool up to 2% of annual committed value for infra outages > agreed thresholds.

If you need a sharper up-front discount, we can exchange that for a faster ramp commitment (e.g., 65/90/100 over three quarters) or introduce a floor consumption guarantee.

Happy to run a quick call tomorrow to align numbers.

—Ben

----
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@ecosense.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual committed pricing vs quarterly billing

Thanks Priya and Ben — this lays out a lot of useful options. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance: 

1) Procurement asks for a one-time early-termination schedule that limits liability if we materially underutilize the committed amount. They suggested an approach where a portion of the committed spend rolls forward as credits rather than being forfeited.
2) Finance wants the true-up to be monthly (we can absorb the admin) instead of quarterly for tighter cash forecasts.
3) Legal will run redlines on Redwood_Terms_v3.docx — we'll share those tomorrow (we've already flagged the SLA credit cap and the termination mechanics).

Attached: Ecosense_Redlines_0624.pdf (high level redlines from Legal)

If Redwood is amenable to a one-off concession on break protection (credit roll-forward for first two quarters) and moves true-up to monthly, we can accelerate to a signature target of July 9. Otherwise procurement wants a fallback plan to stay quarterly billing for the remainder of this year.

—Liam

Attachment: Ecosense_Redlines_0624.pdf (pdf)

----
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@ecosense.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual committed pricing vs quarterly billing

Liam — thank you, this is constructive. Next steps from Redwood: 

- Commercial: we will produce a final pricing worksheet that models: (i) 12- and 24-month commit lines, (ii) monthly true-up vs quarterly true-up scenarios, (iii) credit roll-forward protections for Q1–Q2 underutilization. Expect the spreadsheet this afternoon.
- Legal: we'll incorporate your redlines into our standard terms and explicitly call out the early-termination credit roll-forward (limited to credits covering up to 50% of underutilized committed value for the first two quarters).
- SLOs: we will include the remediation / credit schedule (cap 2% of annual committed value) and add a clause for expedited root-cause response for production-impacting incidents.
- Timeline: Priya/Ben/Aditya will turn around the final SOW + pricing workbook by COB Monday (2026-06-28). If that looks good, we can schedule a procurement + legal sync for July 1 and aim to sign by July 9 per your timeline.

I'll attach the draft workbook now: Final_Pricing_0625.xlsx. Please confirm availability for a 30-minute call on July 1 (10:00 AM PT suggested).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Commercial Manager | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: Final_Pricing_0625.xlsx
